sh: Five EU states plan Rwanda deportation hub
headline: Five EU countries plan a centre in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers
summary: Germany, Austria, Denmark, Greece and the Netherlands announced on Monday 16 November a plan for a joint deportation centre in Rwanda. It would be the first such facility outside the European Union.
why: Migration is one of the biggest political issues in Europe. The plan shows governments moving to tougher rules, while critics say it could weaken protections for vulnerable people.

event.t: The five countries presented the plan in Vienna on Monday 16 November. It would be the first deportation centre of its kind outside the EU.
The centre is meant for people who have no right to stay and cannot be sent back to their own country, for example because that country refuses to take them back.
The scheme is still being negotiated with Rwanda. People sent there could return home, settle in Rwanda or go to another country where they have a right to stay, Rwanda’s government said.
It would start in 2027 as a pilot with about 100 places.
Rights groups condemned the plan, saying it would leave vulnerable people at risk of abuse.

effects.label: Rejected asylum seekers
effects.t: People who cannot be sent home could be moved to Rwanda instead.

effects.label: EU politics
effects.t: Centrist governments are toughening migration rules as support for far-right parties grows, CNN reports.
